messages:
alex: quick sync — i'm primary for the swing this evening (18:00-02:00 PT). planning to watch rolling deploys and keep an eye on latency dashboards. ping me for anything noisy.

mona: noted — i'll be secondary until 23:30, then taylor takes over. calendar overlap is missing 30m (23:30-00:00) due to travel. we should plan a warm handoff or an on-call swap.

taylor: i can cover the 23:45-02:00 section if needed, just FYI i have a short meeting at 23:50 (10m). prefer warm handoff at 23:40.

alex: ok let's do a warm handoff at 23:40. if anyone can't make it we follow the fallback: page the secondary, then sre-lead after 15m.

ryan: small ask — we still have the new prefix-cache rollout on prod at 20:30. suggest we set a temporary higher alert threshold for 30m to avoid noisy pages for expected token-lag.

alex: ++ good call. i'll mute the cache-alert channel for 20:25-21:00 and post a note in #incidents. leave pages on for 5xx and latency>1.5s.

devops-bot: Incident Bot: Scheduled deployment: prefix-cache v2 to prod at 20:30 UTC-07:00. Alerts: CACHE_LATENCY, ROUTER_5XX. Automated noise-suppression ON (20m).

mona: paging rules recap — copy of quick checklist for tonight: 1) Sev1 (customer-impacting outage): page primary + sre-lead immediately and call bridge. 2) Sev2 (major degradations): page primary immediately; if no ack in 5 minutes, page secondary; if no ack in 15 minutes, page sre-lead. 3) Sev3 (minor impact): notify primary via DM; escalate if persists >30m.

alex: adding exact pager names for the rotation: primary = alex (velocity-pager), secondary = mona (velocity-pager-backup), on-call lead = sre-lead (sre-manager-pager). Phone escalation only for Sev1 after 2 minutes with no response.

katie: quick runbook pointers: use runbook link https://confluence.redwood.local/runbooks/inference-degradation — steps 0-5 are triage + mitigation. common quick fixes: flush kv-cache, restart router pods, bump batch window. I left the exact kubectl snippets there.

alex: copying the important snippets here for quick paste:
```
# check router errors
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=router | tail -n 200
# restart router pods one at a time
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/router
# flush prefix cache (internal API)
curl -X POST "https://internal-api/redwood/cache/flush" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

ryan: note about customer impact classification: if >5% requests for top 10 customers hit 500s for >2min -> classify as Sev1 and page managers. we should confirm thresholds with support at start of shift.

mona: agreed. i'll DM support to confirm escalation contact list and update the runbook link with a direct contact table.

alex: coverage gap plan: taylor will join bridge at 23:40 for warm handoff. if taylor can't join, mona please escalate to sre-lead at 23:35 to arrange temporary overlap.

taylor: ack — i'll be in bridge by 23:38. if i'm late, i'll post in this thread and @alex.

devops-bot: Alert muted: CACHE_LATENCY (20:25-21:00).

alex: last bit — on escalation etiquette: when paging sre-lead, include: 1) short summary (what, when, impact), 2) customer list if known, 3) actions taken, 4) link to logs/dashboards. use this subject template: [SEV{1|2}] <service> <short-desc> <region>. saves time.

katie: also — if we need to fallback to older model variant (quantized v1) for capacity reasons, follow the rollback checklist in the runbook (section 3). don't forget to tag the deploy so optimize can reconcile metrics.

mona: will add the phone numbers to the runbook and post a short note in #incidents at 23:20 reminding everyone of the warm handoff.

alex: thanks team. i'll start the deploy-watch at 20:25. ping here for status. :raised_hands:

(timeline note) alex: 1799999999 root message posted
(timeline note) last reply 1800001199 — handoff confirmed and rules noted
